To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a GDL in a PEFC can be quantitatively visualised using synchroton X-ray micro-computert tomography, the porosity distribution in the GDL is heterogeneous and the cyclic porosity variation of the GDL can be observed under freeze-and-thraw cycles.
the adaptive threshold method is superior to the conventional threshold method in three-dimensional reconstruction of a GDL and that the porosity of a GDL is decreased by freeze-and-thaw cycling.

the adaptive threshold method provides more precise three-dimensional reconstruction of the GDL than Otsu's conventional method, that the porosity distribution in the GDL is affected by structural defects, and that the porosity of GDL is cyclically changed under repetitive freeze-and-thaw processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification and analysis of the GDL structure in a PEFC.
the quantitative visualization of the GDL in a PEFC.
the quantification of the GDL using synchroton X-ray imaging techniques and the visualization of its porosity variations under freeze-and-thraw cycles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the porosity of a PEFC GDL is affected not only by the structure but also by the freeze-and-thaw cycle.
the porosity variation is affected by the structural defects and repetitive cycles.
the adaptive threshold method can be effectively used to quantitatively visualize a three-dimensional structure of a GDL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adaptive threshold method is superior to the conventional method, and that the porosity of a GDL is affected by structural defects, as well as freeze-and-thaw conditions.
the porosity distribution and the spatial variation of the porosity in the GDL can be quantitatively visualised using synchrotrons X-ray micro-computert tomography.
the adaptive threshold method is more effective than Otsu's thresholding method for three-dimensional reconstruction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GDL porosity can be quantitatively evaluated using synchroton X-ray micro-computer tomography.
the GDL porosity can be quantitatively and non-invasively measured using the proposed method.
the adaptive threshold method is more suitable for three-dimensional reconstruction than the conventional method.
